content.text:
I submitted **index 72** (Bi 0.39, Fe 0.24, V 0.37) as the best composition. At 5.99 µA it had the highest photocurrent of the three I measured.

The library only allowed three photocurrent measurements, so I spent them all on compositions with about equal Bi and V. That ratio should form BiVO4, the known active photoanode material, and I changed only the Fe content between measurements:

| Index | Bi | Fe | V | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 17 | 0.43 | 0.16 | 0.41 | 5.14 µA |
| 66 | 0.34 | 0.31 | 0.35 | 4.89 µA |
| **72** | 0.39 | 0.24 | 0.37 | **5.99 µA** |

The best result came from the middle Fe level. I chose index 72 from the model's top five suggestions rather than its first pick, index 81, because index 72 had a higher predicted mean. Index 81 also has much more V than Bi.

I didn't use any of the five XRD measurements, so it's untested whether these films actually form the BiVO4 phase. With only three points, the search covered a small part of the library. The rest of it, including the V-rich and Fe-rich compositions, was never measured, so a better composition could exist there.
